purpose: Make dependency-security results reproducible, auditable, and actionable, including the current transitive yanked bisync finding and advisory exceptions.
scope: Cargo audit/deny configuration and lockfile policy, advisory database update behavior, exception records, and remediation tracking. This is a supply-chain control track, not a license-policy redesign.
non_goals: Promising an immediate upstream replacement for every transitive dependency.
Suppressing a finding merely because it is transitive or development-only.
Adding runtime telemetry or network access to production binaries.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Security CI records the advisory database revision and tool version used for each result, and its behavior is deterministic enough that a maintainer can reproduce a pass or failure from the recorded inputs. Network/update failures are reported distinctly from a clean audit.

Every active advisory, yanked-package, or license exception has a structured justification naming the affected dependency path, owner or tracking issue, creation date, expiry/review date, and compensating control. CI fails when an exception expires or its dependency path no longer matches the lockfile.

The transitive bisync yanked-package finding is resolved by a compatible dependency update or retained only under an explicit bounded exception meeting AC-002. The release documentation identifies the chosen state; an untracked yanked package cannot remain a silent warning.

The audit command used locally and in CI is documented as one supported task-runner entry point, emits machine-readable results suitable for artifact retention, and keeps secret values out of logs and artifacts.
